subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Kevlar: The Fabric That Stops Bullets
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Kevlar: The Fabric That Stops Bullets.

hook.text: Kevlar is five times stronger than steel by weight. It was invented by accident in 1965.

buildup.text: Stephanie Kwolek at DuPont was trying to make lightweight tire cord. She got a strange, cloudy liquid instead.

discovery.text: When spun into fiber, the liquid formed chains that aligned perfectly — creating extraordinary tensile strength.

twist.text: Kwolek's supervisor almost threw the liquid away. She insisted on testing it. The result changed body armor forever.

climax.text: Kevlar now protects soldiers, firefighters, and astronauts. It's also in racing tires and suspension cables.

punchline.text: A failed experiment saves lives every day.

quiz.question: How was Kevlar discovered?
options: Military researchers designed it specifically for body armor
Stephanie Kwolek found it accidentally while developing tire cord
It was reverse-engineered from a spider silk study
